newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mazda says no plan to alter ties with Kia Motors.
newsitem.headline: Mazda says no plan to alter ties with Kia Motors.

text.p: Mazda Motor Corp said on Wednesday that it has no plan to change its business relationship with troubled South Korean carmaker Kia Motors Corp, in which the Japanese automaker has a 7.52 percent stake.

"We don't have any plans to change our tie-up with Kia," a Mazda spokesman told Reuters. He said Mazda has no plan to cut its stake in the company, adding that Mazda has not received a request from Kia Motors for financial support.

Mazda, owned 33.4 percent by Ford Motor Co, delivers knockdown parts to Kia Motor for the assembly of cars and commercial vehicles such as Kia's Pride and Luce models, but Mazda did not disclose how many sets of these knockdown parts it sends to Kia.

On Tuesday, South Korean banks stepped in to rescue the Kia Group, the country's eighth largest business conglomerate, whose carmaking flagship has been battered by slumping sales. The Kia Group had total debts of 9.54 trillion won ($10.7 billion) at the end of May, according to the Korea Federation of Banks.

Mazda said it cannot immediately estimate to what extent Mazda's business will be affected by Kia's financial trouble. Analysts say Kia's woes may not hurt Mazda's business, but some warn they could slash Mazda's sales.

"I see no big impact on Mazda because even if Kia Motors goes under, vehicle production using Mazda's knockdown parts will continue at the carmaker which takes over Kia," said Koji Endo, a senior vice president of Lehman Brothers Japan Inc.
"Mazda's holdings in Kia shares may become useless but Mazda's holdings are worth only seven or eight billion yen, a negligible loss."

But Seiji Sugiura, a senior analyst at Nomura Securities Co Ltd, said in a report on Wednesday that Mazda's shares may see selling pressure which could push them down to around 280-300 yen. On Wednesday, Mazda's shares ended down four yen at 376 yen.
In the worst case scenario, Nomura Securities said it estimates that Mazda's sales could fall by some 30-35 billion yen.
